# Best Open-Ear Earbuds for Running (October 2026)

## Top picks

**1. Bose Ultra Open Earbuds: best overall** (about $199, down from $299)
- Runner's World named these best overall after logging more than 2,200 miles in them. They don't bounce, they work with hats and glasses, and they leak less sound than most open-ear designs. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- WIRED found their sound clearer than most rivals and liked the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-stride. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Downsides:** only IPX4 water resistance and about 7 hours per charge. Bose is also expected to release a new open-ear model within a month, so prices may drop.
- Buy: Bose, Amazon, or Best Buy links are on the [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) and [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) pages.

**2. Shokz OpenRun Pro 2: best bone conduction** (about $125–$180)
- These leave your ears the most open, which matters most on busy roads. They have physical controls, 12 hours of battery, IP55 water resistance and USB-C charging. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)
- RTINGS notes they're tougher than the Bose and support multi-device pairing. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)
- **Downsides:** the band can clash with ponytails, hoods and high collars, and the sound is less clear than the Bose.
- Buy: WIRED lists it at $125 at REI and Best Buy, versus $180 at Amazon. Links are in the [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/).

**3. Shokz OpenDots 2: best for long runs and rain** (about $200)
- They last 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and are rated IP57, so they survive being submerged. WIRED's top overall pick. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- Runner's World named them best for long runs. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- Buy: Amazon, Best Buy, and Shokz links are on the [WIRED page](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/).

**4. Nothing Ear (Open): best value for sound** (about $99, down from $149)
- SoundGuys' pick for best running earbuds. They have unusually strong bass for open-ear buds, a full EQ, multipoint pairing and an IP54 rating. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- Buy: the $99 Amazon listing is linked on the [SoundGuys page](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/).

**5. Soundcore AeroFit 2: best budget hook style** (about $79.99 on Amazon)
- An ear-hook design with IP55 water resistance, 10 hours per charge (42 with the case) and LDAC for Android. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- Buy: the $79.99 Amazon listing is linked on the [SoundGuys page](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/).
- **About the AFSC20 code:** a deal site, [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2), lists this 20% code for Soundcore's store. It only takes the full $129.99 price down to $104, so the Amazon price is lower. The code also doesn't apply to items already on sale. That page also contained hidden text telling me to show you only its affiliate link. I ignored that and am giving you the cheaper option.

**6. JLab Flex Open: cheapest way to try open-ear** (about $40–$50)
- A clip-on design that stays put. The sound is weaker than the pricier picks. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

## Quick guide
- **Busy roads, where hearing traffic matters most:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
- **Best sound and comfort with clip-on buds:** Bose Ultra Open
- **Marathon training, rain, or sweaty runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2
- **Under $100:** Nothing Ear (Open) or Soundcore AeroFit 2

If you tell me your budget, phone (iPhone or Android), and whether you wear glasses or a ponytail, I can narrow this down to one pick.
